gaps.sentence: She suggested ___ the meeting until Monday.

gaps.explanation: seem/appear take the to-infinitive: seems to know.

gaps.sentence: He apologised for ___ so rude to the waiter.
gaps.explanation: 'Apologise for being' — 'for' is a preposition, so the gerund follows.

gaps.sentence: We're looking forward to ___ from you soon.
gaps.explanation: 'Look forward to + -ing' — 'to' is a preposition, so the gerund follows.

gaps.sentence: The teacher advised us ___ the essay twice.
gaps.explanation: advise + object + to-infinitive: advised us to check. (advise + -ing is possible without object: advise checking.)

gaps.sentence: After introducing herself, she went on ___ the main findings.
gaps.hint: move on to a new activity
gaps.explanation: go on + to-infinitive = do something after finishing something else.

gaps.sentence: I really can't afford ___ on holiday this year.
gaps.explanation: afford takes the to-infinitive: can't afford to go.
